body:
## Problem

Highlight inspection is limited to a single position, and its result types
do not document the fields shared by different highlight sources.

## Solution

Accept `end_row`/`end_col` in `vim.inspect_pos()` to return items overlapping
a range with an exclusive end. Empty ranges return no items. Omitting the
end preserves single-position inspection. `:Inspect` accepts Ex line
ranges, including Visual selections.

Document the result types and their range and highlight fields. Extmarks
and semantic tokens expose `hl_group`/`hl_group_link` at the top level while
retaining the existing `opts` fields for compatibility.

comment_data.body: any reason not to inline these? by "naming" them in docs we are taking on some api surface area

I don't think so. The result of `inspect_pos` returns a different table for each type. In this PR these types are unified a bit so every table also has a `hl_group` and `hl_group_link` field. This standardisation is represented by the parent of each of these classes. This is important as it means the user can iterate the subtables and rely on the common fields, e.g. for transfering highlights to virtual_lines/text.

And really anything with ~4 or more fields really deserves it's own type.

If we really want to simplify this, then we need to unify the returned table types, but even then it becomes tricky.

And fwiw, I have in the past found the lack of documentation for these return values difficult to work with. You end up having to run the functiona interactively to learn what they look like.
Turned into a type so it can be reused in lua.txt

comment_regular_data.body:
@lewis6991 just making a note here in case it's useful: tree-sitter v0.26.5

> introduces a new API ts_query_cursor_set_containing_{byte,point}_range, which can be used to restrict the query cursor to search for matches where all nodes fall into (instead of merely overlap) a given range. This enables much more aggressive optimizations that can resolve performance issues, e.g., with extremely long lines.
